ch08.p.d.path: Path along which the particle is moved from A to B
ch08.p.d.force: Force whose work is computed: gravity or a spring (conservative), kinetic friction (nonconservative)
ch08.p.d.closed: After reaching B, return to A in a straight line
ch08.p.goal.cons: Conservative force: the work between two points does not depend on the path; around a closed path it is zero
ch08.p.goal.fric: Kinetic friction always opposes the motion, so its work is proportional to the path length: nonconservative
ch08.p.obs.same: Gravity and spring: the cumulative-work curves of the four paths differ in shape, but all end on the same dashed line
ch08.p.obs.closed: Closed path: back at the start, gravity and the spring have done $W = 0$; kinetic friction has done $W < 0$
ch08.p.obs.fric: Kinetic friction: $W$ keeps falling in proportion to the path length $s$; the zigzag ends most negative
ch08.p.obs.custom: Drag a waypoint: drag the orange circle to change the path; the end value for a conservative force stays put
ch08.p.assume: Mass 1 kg moved at a steady 1.5 m/s (other forces control the motion), A $= (-2, 0)$ m, B $= (2, 1.5)$ m, spring $k = 2$ N/m (natural length 0, fixed end at $(0, -1.5)$ m), $\mu_k = 0.5$
ch08.e.d.friction: A kinetic friction force of 0.15 N acts, so the mechanical energy decreases
ch08.e.goal.read: Energy diagram: the gap between the $U(x)$ curve and the total-energy line $E$ is the kinetic energy $K = E - U$
ch08.e.goal.force: Force = minus the slope of the potential curve, $F = -dU/dx$, always toward lower $U$
ch08.e.obs.const: No friction: $K$ and $U$ trade places but $E$ stays constant (bars, graph)
ch08.e.obs.turn: Turning points: where $U = E$ and $K = 0$ the motion reverses. The grey regions ($U > E$) cannot be entered
ch08.e.obs.eq: Equilibrium points $dU/dx = 0$: a minimum is stable (filled dot), a maximum is unstable (open dot)
ch08.e.obs.drag: Drag the particle to change where it starts (at rest): in the double well, start above the hump to visit both wells. Well and hill: once over the hill it escapes to the left
ch08.e.obs.friction: Friction on: the $E$ line sinks and the turning points close in, until the particle stops in a well
ch08.e.assume: Mass 1 kg, motion in one dimension, starts at rest, kinetic friction of constant size (when on)
